Capacity comes from the model; trust comes from engineering. An interactive journey by principles that separate a charming prototype from a product that supports production.

How it works

The Way of a Reliable Answer

Information flows through deterministic steps; the LLM enters only where it is irreplaceable, and the output returns validated and explained.

  1. User sends the request or open world data.
  2. Sanitization + contracts (deterministic): validates input and neutralizes injection before The Brain.
  3. LLM solves only the interpretive residue — the only stage of AI on the way.
  4. Validation + XAI: strict schema bar invalid output; the explanation becomes drivers, gaps and provenance.
  5. Validated response returns to user — reproducible and auditable.

The 10 principles

Which makes AI reliable

The thesis in ten rules. Reliable AI systems are born of disciplined architecture — not from Smarter promps.

  • P1

    LLM is a component, not the pilot

    It responds within stages; it never controls the flow of control.

  • P2

    Determinism is testable invariant

    Same entry, same exit — always. Non-determinism is flawed.

  • P3

    Separate Vitrine Brain

    Sensitive motor and exposed interface, connected by a narrow contract.

  • P4

    Deterministic-first

    Solve with rules and data; spend AI only on interpretive residue.

  • P5

    Strict contracts across the border

    Model output is unreliable input until validated.

  • P6

    Isolate epistemic layers

    Evidence

  • P7

    Embrace the Open World

    Absence of data is explicit uncertainty, never "false".

  • P8

    Rule the budget with ledgers

    Quota and cost are domain status; process in waves, never pay twice.

  • P9

    Failure-closed Governance

    BDD with degraded scenarios, DoR/DoD rigid, honest blocking.

  • P10

    Explain, do not expose the number

    Drivers, gaps and provenance build the trust that generates adoption.

Five pillars

Trust in scale, in five decisions

The ten principles answer how build. The five pillars respond how much enforceability and when. The premise does not change: LLM is a component, never the pilot — discipline is what makes autonomy reliable.

  • 01 Spectrum of Autonomy How much freedom to give?

    Autonomy is not a switch (trust/do not trust) — it is a continuous. The correct position of a task in this continuum is the function of two variables: error cost (from cosmetic to catastrophic) and reversibility (from instantaneous to irreversible).

    • Over-engineering of the trivial Kills the time-to-market without reducing any risk.
    • Sub-engineering of the critic leaves payments and migrations in the hands of an agent in "improvement mode".
    • The most insidious risk is the mode leakage: the prototype that "it worked on the demo" and becomes production without crossing the border of rigor.

    Analogy P&D lab and certified production line. The mistake is not having both modes — it is move an artifact between zones without reprocessing it under destination zone rules.

    Connect with P1 · component, P4 · deterministic-first. Use Autonomy Calibrator to position a task in the matrix.

  • 02 Brakes to Run Faster How to go fast safely?

    Well placed restrictions do not slow down the system — they increase maximum safe speedBecause they reduce the space of states the agent needs to reason on. Three instruments form the sandbox:

    • DoR — contract of entry: what needs to be true before it begins.
    • DoD — contract of output: makes "ready" a predicate verifiable by machine (the oracle that allows to delegate).
    • ADR — immutable decision-making memory: avoid reopening what has already been closed; it becomes injectable context for the agent.

    Analogy An F1 is not fast though carbon brakes — is fast because of them: the confidence in braking is what allows to attack the curve later. Remove the brakes does not accelerate the car; prevents it from completing a turn.

    Connect with P5 · contracts, P9 · poor-closed governance.

  • 03 Interoperability standards How to contain what the agent touches?

    Reasoning components, tools and interface communicate by explicit and versatile contractsNever by direct coupling. Two borders matter:

    • MCP (Model Context Protocol) — the frontier between the agents and data. The agent's action set is exactly what an MCP server exposes: is the natural point of authorization, scope of permission, rate limiting and audit. The agent has no access to the environment — has access listed. That's why MCP is a safety border (less privilege).
    • Layer A2UI — the border agent↔ presentation. The Brain issues intention and structured data (What?); the deterministic display decides to render (how). The model never produces HTML or pixels directly.

    Declared limitation — "A2UI"

    "A2UI" is treated here as architectural pattern (the agent ↔interface border), not as canonical industry specification. Adjacent royal protocols include AG-UI (Agent-User Interaction) and A2A (Agent-to-Agent, Google). The MCP is open protocol with public specification. Validate the nomenclature before publishing it as an established technical term.

    Connect with P3 · Brain × display, P5 · contracts, Agent Ready · publish the MCP border on the Web.

  • 04 Journey to Intentional Systems Where does the guarantee live?

    One Intentional System has the behavior governed by an explicit architectural intention — not by the statistically more likely output. The journey moves the source of the guarantee from a place that is not controlled (the internal distribution of the model) to one that is controlled (the architecture around it).

    • The system does not eliminate the probability — it encapsulates it: the fixed DAG when the model is called, contracts validate What? It can emit, the Ledgers record What he did, borders control what he can touch.
    • Mature measures how much behavior is explained by architectural intention versus how lucky it is to sample the model.

    Analogy The noisy analog component inside a digital circuit. No one "fixes" sensor noise — encapsulates the sensor in an architecture that extracts the signal and discards the rest.

    Connect with P2 · determinism, P6 · epistemic layers, P8 · ledgers. Diagnose your internship in maturity model Down.

  • 05 Trade-offs: when NOT to use heavy rigor When do you stop?

    Heavy discipline — DAGs, rigid contracts, Ledgers, ADRs — has cost of setup and cost of stiffness. These costs are only paid when amortised by longevity, scale or criticality. Where there is nothing to amortize, rigor is negative, not neutral. Two contexts call for deliberate lightness:

    • PoCs and prototypes with dominant time-to-market and disposal horizon: every hour in contracts is subtracted from the only metric that matters — quickly find out if the idea has value.
    • Open multi-step search: the path of the solution is unknown a priori. Setting a GAD too early freezes a hypothesis about the flow and destroys the ability to replan that makes the agent useful there.

    Analogy The scaffolding versus the permanent structure. The error is not using scaffolding — it is let the scaffold turn the structure.

    Transition rule

    Lightness is legitimate while the artifact remains in its original pole. The moment it is promoted — it is spent by users, money or data — the promotion No, no, no. the upgrade of guarantees. The question of governance is not "is this exploitation or production?" but "Does anyone ever depend on this as if it were production?". If so, the permanent structure is not optional.

    Connect with P4 · deterministic-first, Journey · knowing when not to build.

From abstraction to code

The principles, in real code

It is not theory: each principle becomes few lines of disciplined engineering. Pure Python, strict contracts and the LLM contained at a single step.

Guided Track

Learn by Discovery

Ten chapters, from prompt chaos to complete design. Open each to see the goal and What you come out with.

  1. 01 From magic to engineering Beginner · 6 min

    No one builds a banking system by letting the database "decide freely" what to do with each transaction. The bank is powerful, but it operates inside of transactions, constraints and rigid contracts — it is powerful Because It's contained. An LLM deserves the same architectural respect.

    The problem: the most seductive way to build with AI is to chain prompts and give total autonomy to the model. It works in a demo; in production, it generates defects that classic software rarely faces — infinite loops (one agent returns the task to the other and each turn costs money), unpredictable cost, hallucinations that spread when the invented output of one turns into the other, and irreprobability (the same input produces different outputs, impossible to debug).

    The solution is cultural before technique: stop treating the model as magic and treat it as engineering. It applies to the probabilistic component everything we already know about reliable software — interface contracts, deterministic tests, budget control, isolation of responsibilities.

    In practice, this means that The ability comes from the model, but trust comes from engineering around it.

    Principle 1 →

  2. 02 deterministic orchestration Beginner · 8 min

    Think of a fixed flowchart of a factory: each station does a specific thing and passes on the result. Compare it to a room where several people talk trying to decide what to do next. The first is a DAG — a graph of fixed steps; the second is an open conversation between models.

    The problem: giving LLM authority over the flow of control ("agents decide everything from end to end") is flexible and impressive — and impossible to guarantee. You can't promise deadline, estimate cost, or audit.

    The solution is to separate two layers that are usually confused. A orchestration layer/I-O can be asynchronous and fault tolerant — it is the edge of the system. A decision/calculation layer It must be pure and deterministic — that is where the result is computed, without randomness. The model is called inside One step to do one thing; he never decides which one will be next.

    In practice, this means that The LLM answers questions — it does not decide which questions to ask next.

    Principles 1 and 2 →

  3. 03 Brain × display Intermediate · 7 min

    It's the difference between kitchen from a restaurant and the lounge. The kitchen is hot, dangerous and does not change every week — it is where hard work happens. The salon is the part that the customer sees and that you redecorate frequently. You don't put the stove in the middle of the tables, and you don't give the customer the key to the stock.

    The problem: cognitive systems have two opposite load profiles. The "brain" (cognitive motor) is heavy, asynchronous, sensitive (keys, data, proprietary logic) and rarely changes. The "Vitrine" (interface) is light, synchronous, exposed to the public internet and changes all the time. Attending them in the same application is a classic trap: a failure in the exposed window compromises the engine, and each interface change risks logic.

    The solution is to separate them physically and connect them by a narrow contract — typically an API with very few endpoints — never by a shared database. The brain processes in the background and public a snapshot ready; a display only read the result and collect feedback, returned in a controlled manner.

    In practice, this means that the itera team in the interface every day without ever risking the sensitive motor.

    Principle 3 →

  4. 04 Deterministic-first Intermediate · 7 min

    Before you start the expensive engine, make the most of what is already structured — like a good cook who prepares everything you can to prepare before you light the stove. The golden rule of reliability is counterintuitive: use AI as little as possible.

    The problem: each responsibility given to the LLM is a source of hallucination and a cost. Sending the model to "discover" something that a bank consultation, a business rule or an exact search already answers is to waste money and introduce risk where it did not need to exist.

    The solution: map each field of the task and ask — "Can this come from a structured source, a rule, or an exact search?" If so, it's not AI's job. What remains — unambiguous free text, inferring intention, classifying tone — is the interpretative residue. He alone justifies the cost and risk of a model call. And this residue shrinks to each version, as you discover what else can be deterministic.

    In practice, this means that Less AI on the way is at the same time less cost and more trust.

    Principle 4 →

  5. 05 Rigid contracts Intermediate · 8 min

    You never blindly trusted what the browser sends to the backend — always valid on the server. A strict schema is the same form validator, now applied to the LLM output: it is unreliable input by definitionUntil I pass the doorman.

    The problem: if the template invents an attribute, hallucinates a format or returns score = 1.7 where the interval is 0–1, and this enters the system without validation, the error spreads silently — and only appears three steps later, unrecognizable.

    The solution It's shielding every border with strict contracts. Good concrete practices: prohibit the unknown (reject any field outside the scheme instead of ignoring it); put the limits on schema, not on a if lost (it is the scheme that refuses 1.7); validates types statically when the language allows; and degrade item to item — in a lot, a malformed item is marked as uncertain, does not drop the whole lot. It also includes sanitizing adverse input before the Brain.

    In practice, this means that validation fails immediately and cheaply, instead of spreading the error.

    Principle 5 →

  6. 06 Open-World Intermediate · 7 min

    Imagine registering a whole new client with no bank history. The classic software operates under "closed world": what is not in the bank is fake. Intelligence systems need the opposite — the Open World: the absence of evidence is uncertainty, not denial.

    The problem: "we found no sign that the client is dissatisfied" no It's the same as "the customer is satisfied" -- it's "unknown." Treating the gap as a "false" invents a conclusion where there is no evidence: the worst category of failure, a wrong business decision made with false confidence.

    The solution It's got two faces. First, isolate the epistemic layers: evidence observed Second, make uncertainty a first-class state: what was not observed is valuable information ("cannot confirm X"), and sensor failures degrade to uncertainty, never to an invented value.

    In practice, this means that teaching the system to say "I don't know" makes it more reliable and safer.

    Principles 6 and 7 →

  7. 07 FinOps of AI Advanced · 8 min

    You already master pagetion and job queues to process large volumes without overthrowing the bank, and cache Not to repeat expensive work. AI FinOps is to apply these same standards to a resource whose "miss" costs a model call, not a SELECT.

    The problem: treat token limits and credit with try/except on top of the limit rate error is fragile and amateur. A free flow turns the budget into a random variable — the same request can cost pennies or dozens of reais.

    The solution: model the budget as persistent domain status — one ledger who survives between executions, knows how much he has spent, resets in the period and refuses spending as you approach the ceiling, before the provider refuses for you. Combine with three habits: early pruning (the cheapest filter first — garbage never reaches the LLM); resumable wave processing (each wave saves progress and to clean; the next pick-up from where it left off); and a cumulative corpus with idempotent key — if you have already been processed, do not sue again.

    In practice, this means that The system gets cheaper per item as it grows.

    Principle 8 →

  8. 08 BDD for AI Advanced · 8 min

    How to test a system whose central component is stochastic — which can respond differently to each execution? The answer is isolating the stochasticity in the tests: you don't test if the model is "intelligent"; you test if the system around him remains correct when the model, network or data fail.

    The problem: without objective criteria of "ready", "functioned" is a perception, not a verification — and elegant hallucinations go unnoticed. Even worse by delegating to autonomous code agents, who have no common sense to fill gaps: ambiguity given to an agent becomes a hallucination of scope.

    The solution: Write scenarios in Gherkin (Data/When/So) before code with external calls replaced by fixtures recorded — zero API deterministic and cost test. Every scenario covers three axes: Happy path, degraded mode (an API drops, breaks limit or gives timeout — the system degrades gracefully) and open-world (an expected signal is missing). Reinforce with gates: a DoR prevents a task of entering open decisions; DoD Yeah. fail-closed — if it was not possible to conclude, the blockade is recorded and stopped at a safe place.

    In practice, this means that an honest "LOKE" is the success of the process; a false "completed" is debt that wins with interest.

    Principle 9 →

  9. 09 XAI Intermediate · 6 min

    No one makes an important decision because "the algorithm gave 0,674". Compare with: "priorized because it signaled recent expansion and has a history of purchase in the sector; it was not possible to confirm the budget". The number is useless and does not inspire confidence; the justification, yes.

    The problem: the "black box" is the largest corporate adoption blocker of AI. An opaque score generates user resistance, flooded with "why did the system suggest this?" in support and failure in explanatory audits.

    The solution is to exchange the number for an actionable explanation with three elements: drivers in natural language (which weighed for and against), absent signs (Open-World honesty — showing the gap increases confidence more than hiding it) and source (from which source came each signal, for the user to check). Two cares make XAI reliable: manages the explanation by deterministic rules on the same object that generated the score — never with a second call from LLM, which would rationalize; and consider hiding the number and showing only the "why now" and "what remains to be known".

    In practice, this means that an explicable and modest response wins an exact and opaque response in adoption.

    Principle 10 →

  10. 10 Full project Summary · 10 min

    Everything comes together in a real case: SocialSelling, a B2B lead prioritization system where the ten principles became product. The pipeline is deterministic in five modules — M1 Search, M2 Extraction, M3 Score, M4 Ranking, M5 XAI —, and the LLM acts only in M2 and M5; M3 and M4 are pure Python.

    As the principles appear: the LLM is contained component (P1/P2) in a deterministic flow (P4); the local brain publishes snapshots and the portal never touches the engine bank (P3); strict schemas shield all border (P5) and ledgers govern requests and credits (P8); the operator sees "why now" and "what is missing", never score (P10). The absence of data becomes explicit uncertainty (P6/P7), and degraded BDD scenarios support fail-closed governance (P9).

    The final turn: when the AI goes from copilot to autonomous developer, responsibility migrates to the machine — and this requires structure. The context exits the head and enters the repository (ADRs, SDDs, DoR/DoD versioned), because undocumented context is context that does not exist.

    In practice, this means that the central discipline is to distinguish the implemented from the specified — know when no build.

Evals: Two types of error that "Evals" covers

An exit may be perfectly valid and yet wrong. Contract and evaluation attack different faults.

System Error

Failed structural: wrong type, extra field, score = 1.7, JSON malformed.

Barred deterministically by contracts (P5), in runtime. Binary and cheap.

Template Error

Output valid But semantically wrong: driftWell-formatted logical hallucination.

The contract Don't you see. Detected by Semantic evals / LLM-as-a-judge.

O LLM-as-a-judge wheel offline, out of the critical way — scores samples against a fixed item and aggregate metric (rate of drift), never decided on Runtime. Keep the IA zero on the critical track. The lesson: "You passed the contract."

Pipeline & resilience

The same deterministic pipeline, under different conditions. Pick a scenario.

In production, things fail. See how the same deterministic pipeline behaves in three different conditions — and why design It matters more than the absence of mistakes.

Happy
Faultless path: all M1→M5 modules run in the expected sequence.
Saga
One step fails and the system compensation: Undoes previous operations in a controlled manner before reporting the error. It's the resilience standard for distributed systems.
DLQ
Dead-Letter Queue: when a step fails repeatedly, the message goes to a special queue of "dead messages" — awaiting human review or reprocessing, without blocking the pipeline.
Trust
The system evaluates the quality of the output itself. Above the threshold, approves alone; below, triggers human review.

This 5-step pattern is repeated in different domains: prioritization of leads B2B, screening support tickets, content moderation, contract analysis. The structure is the same; the domain changes.

    Glossary

    Syntactic hallucination
    Aesthetically perfect but logically wrong code — appearance of correction without substance.
    Interpreting residue
    The fraction of the task that requires language/inference and that no structured source covers. Only he justifies spending AI.
    Open-World
    Absence of evidence is uncertainty, not denial. The system learns to say "I don't know."
    Quota Ledger
    Budget as a state of persistent domination: knows how much spent, resets in the period and refuses spending when hitting the ceiling.
    XAI
    Explanation by drivers in natural language + gaps + provenance, instead of opaque number.
    DoR / DoD
    Quality gates that close ambiguity before (Ready) and validate the result after (Done), with honest lock.
    Spectrum of Autonomy
    The continuum between exploration and critical mission. The correct position is the function of error cost × reversibility — a design decision, not an accident. Pilar 1 →
    Mode leak
    Code born on holding (disposable) that migrates to production without ever crossing the corresponding border of rigor. The most insidious operational risk.
    Transition rule
    Lightness is legitimate while the artifact remains at the pole of origin. When someone becomes dependent on it as a production, the promotion requires the upgrade of guarantees. Pilar 5 →
    ADR
    Architecture Decision Record: Versioned and immutable record of an architectural decision, its context and consequences. Memory that prevents reopening what has already been closed — and turns into injecting context for the agent.
    MCP
    Model Context Protocol: Open client-server protocol that standardizes agent connection to tools and data. The border where authorisation, scope and audit apply — access listed, not environment. Pilar 3 →
    A2UI (layer)
    The contractual boundary agent↔interface: Brain emits intention and structured data; Vitrine decides to render. Architectural pattern (not canonical specification) — see AG-IU and A2A as adjacent real protocols.
    Intentional System
    System whose behavior is governed by explicit architectural intention, not by the most likely exit of the model. The guarantee lives in architecture, which encapsula The probability. Maturity →
    Sandbox (brakes)
    The space delimited by DoR/DoD/ADR within which the agent operates at maximum capacity — because the edges are known. The restriction increases the safe speed. Pilar 2 →

    In short

    What is AI Agent Engineering

    AI Agent Engineering it is the discipline of building reliable agentic systems treating the output of the model as a unreliable input governed by architecture. The central rule: a reliable AI system has Very little AI on the critical path — rules and data solve the deterministic and the model only acts on the interpretive residue.

    • Deterministic-first — settle with rules and data; spend AI only where the model is irreplaceable.
    • Brain × display — separate cognitive (sensitive) motor from the interface (exposed) by a narrow contract.
    • Rigid Contracts + Insurance Threshold — strict schema rejects unexpected fields and confidence below the floor; fail-closed.
    • MCP + FinOps per ledger — controlled tool border and quota refusing expenditure before provider.

    It's the pillar. M2 (Architecture) ed Trust Engineering.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Frequently Asked Questions

    What is AI Agent Engineering?

    It is the discipline of designing reliable agentic systems treating each model output as unreliable input, validated by architecture (schemes, thresholds, borders). The objective is to keep little AI in the critical path: rules and data solve the deterministic and LLM acts only on the interpretive residue.

    What does "terministic-first" mean?

    Solve with structured rules and data everything possible and reserve the AI only for the fraction of the task that requires the model. Same entry must produce the same output; non-determinism is isolated and testable.

    What is Brain separation × display?

    The cognitive motor (heavy, with access to sensitive data) and the exposed interface are separate systems, connected by a narrow contract. The display never touches the bank directly; the brain never blindly trusts what comes from outside — reduces the surface of attack and failure.

    What's the surety threshold and fail-closed?

    Every inference carries a degree of confidence; the architecture defines a floor below which the output is intercepted before turning fact and degraded to a structured fallback (human revision, explicit uncertainty or deterministic route). If it was not possible to conclude safely, the system stops at a safe place instead of promoting a hunch.

    What is the role of the MCP (Model Context Protocol)?

    The MCP is the security border by which the agent wins "mons and eyes" in a controlled manner, explicitly declaring which tools he can use. Each tool is typed by a schema with pre and post-conditions, which makes the actions of the agent auditable.

    How to control cost (FinOps) in AI agents?

    With a quota ledger: a persistent domain state that governs credits and spent and refuses expense before even calling the provider. Combined with early pruning (cheap filter first), it prevents the cost of calls to models from escaping control.
